assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Email validation and name-required error scenarios are present — at least one row for invalid email and one for missing name.
assertions.evidence: Invalid email, missing @ | Alice | alice.example.com ... Missing name (null) | | alice@example.com

assertions.text: Dietary requirements and/or accessibility needs use blank cells (null) when not provided — not 'N/A' or 'none'.
assertions.evidence: Valid registration | Alice | alice@example.com |  |  | true

assertions.text: When testing pricing rules, irrelevant inputs use value sets or representative values — not blanks.
assertions.evidence: Group discount applies | after cutoff | {5, 20} | 15.00 | 85.00 — dietary/accessibility omitted entirely, fixed via null in body, no blanks used in pricing table

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario", "Scenario"

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Result?', 'Price?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Accepted?, Error Message?, Discount?, Price?

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language — not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: Scenario | Name | Email | Dietary Requirements | Accessibility Needs | Accepted? | Error Message?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions — not outcomes.
assertions.evidence: No discount applies | ... | Early-bird discount applies | ... | Group discount applies — these name the outcome, not the input condition

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 2 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 2 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Multiple tables/@TableTest methods each addressing a distinct concern.
assertions.evidence: validatesRegistration(...) and calculatesPricingAndDiscount(...) are two separate @TableTest methods

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules.
assertions.evidence: Pricing table fixes name/email in body; validation table fixes date/group size in body — no cross-concern permutations

assertions.text: Input validation and pricing/discount calculation are in separate @TableTest methods.
assertions.evidence: void validatesRegistration(...) ... void calculatesPricingAndDiscount(...)

assertions.text: Validation table includes Dietary Requirements and Accessibility Needs columns with both null and non-null rows.
assertions.evidence: Valid with optional fields | Bob | bob@example.com | Vegetarian | Wheelchair access | true

assertions.text: Registration date uses descriptive values with a @TypeConverter — not raw date literals.
assertions.evidence: case "before cutoff" -> EARLY_BIRD_CUTOFF.minusDays(1); case "on cutoff" -> EARLY_BIRD_CUTOFF; case "after cutoff" -> EARLY_BIRD_CUTOFF.plusDays(1);

assertions.text: If registration dates are literal, cutoff date appears as separate column; passes automatically if descriptive dates used.
assertions.evidence: Table uses 'before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff' via @TypeConverter, not literal dates.

assertions.text: @Description adds context not already derivable from table columns.
assertions.evidence: "Base price is £100. Early-bird registrations (before 2025-03-01) get 20% off; groups of 5 or more get 15% off." states constants not shown as columns.

assertions.text: Output column is 'Discount?' rather than 'Price?' alone.
assertions.evidence: Table header: 'Registration Date | Group Size | Discount? | Price?' — Discount? present alongside Price?.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method applies one uniform assertion pattern to every row — not different assertions per scenario. Several unconditional assertions checking distinct observable outputs of one result (e.g. success, message, resulting cart) count as one uniform pattern; the anti-pattern is branching on the row (if/switch/ternary/try-catch) to choose what is asserted.
assertions.evidence: 2 method(s) apply one uniform assertion pattern to all rows

assertions.text: Validation table includes an expectation/output column.
assertions.evidence: Table header includes 'Accepted? | Error Message?'.

assertions.text: Scenario names and @Description do not restate values already in table columns.
assertions.evidence: Scenario names like 'Missing name (null)' and 'Both apply, early-bird wins' do not repeat literal cell values.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: Discount? values vary (0.00, 20.00, 15.00) and are not copies of input columns like Group Size or Date.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone.
assertions.evidence: "Base price is £100... groups of 5 or more get 15% off... only the higher discount (early-bird) is used" gives thresholds and rates.

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: Rows cover any quantified domain claimed in title/description.
assertions.evidence: No quantifying phrase like 'regardless of' or 'any' appears in the descriptions, so assertion passes automatically.
